newsitem.title: DUBAI: OPEC ministers Aghazadeh, Arrieta meet in Tehran.
newsitem.headline: OPEC ministers Aghazadeh, Arrieta meet in Tehran.

text.p: Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh and Venezuelan Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta met in Tehran on Monday ahead of an OPEC monitoring committee meeting and an energy conference in Isfahan, the English-language Iran News newspaper reported on Tuesday.
"The two ministers reviewed mutual cooperation in fields such as the crude oil sales in markets close to both countries and the petrochemical industry," Iran News reported.

Arrieta is expected to attend a regular two-day meeting of OPEC's ministerial output monitoring committee starting today in Isfahan before addressing an international oil conference in the same Iranian city.
Venezuela is estimated to be OPEC's largest quota violator, pumping some 3.2 million barrels per day (bpd) in recent months versus its quota of 2.359 million bpd.
Total OPEC output in March hit 26.9 million bpd in March, in excess of its agreed quota of 25.03 million bpd, according to Reuters' survey of analysts and industry sources.
Higher OPEC flows has contributed to a downturn in world oil prices which have slumped from $24 a barrel at the start of the year to under $18 this month.
Aghazadeh at last OPEC's ministerial meeting called on OPEC states to strictly observe their quotas.
The two ministers also discussed Venezuela's experience in developing its heavy crude reserves, Iran News reported.
